title: Tapestry crochet
subtitle: Carrying multiple yarn colours inside stitches to build a colour pattern
excerpt: Tapestry crochet works a colour pattern by carrying unused colours inside the stitches rather than cutting and rejoining at each colour block. The technique produces a fabric with the pattern locked into the structure rather than applied on top.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book (Storey Publishing). Pauline Turner, How to Crochet (HarperCollins). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework, 1886, Project Gutenberg #20776.

glossaryTerms.definition: A colourwork technique in which unused yarn colours are carried inside the body of the stitches as you work, creating a dense, double-thickness fabric with a colour pattern embedded in the structure.
A length of yarn carried behind or inside the work when it is not the active colour, without being worked into the stitches.
In colourwork, the colour that is picked up from below tends to sit forward and appears more prominently in the finished fabric.

content.text: Tapestry crochet

builds colour patterns into fabric by carrying unused yarns inside each stitch as you work. The unused colours sit inside the stitch body, hidden from view, instead of being cut and rejoined at each colour change.

The technique works best in double crochet (UK), which gives a compact stitch that hides the carried yarn neatly. It is used for bags, baskets, pouches, and any piece where stiffness is an asset rather than a problem. On garments it can make the fabric heavier than the yarn alone would suggest.
What you need

items.name: DK or aran yarn in two or more colours
items.note: Smooth plied yarns show the pattern most clearly; fuzzy yarns blur colour boundaries

items.name: Crochet hook
items.note: One size smaller than the yarn label recommends, to keep the fabric firm enough to hide the carried strands

items.name: Tapestry needle
items.note: For weaving in tails at colour changes

items.name: Stitch marker
items.note: To mark the beginning of rounds if working in the round

content.text: How it works
The key move is working over the
float

. When you switch to a new colour, pick it up from underneath the colour you are setting aside. The yarn you are setting aside lies along the top of the previous row. As you work the next group of stitches in the new colour, insert the hook, pick up the new colour, and complete the stitch as usual. The carried strand sits inside the stitch, enclosed but not worked.
Worked example: two-colour stripe block
This swatch uses two colours, A and B, in a simple block pattern: four stitches in A, four in B, repeated across the row.
Foundation: ch 17 in colour A. (This gives 16 working stitches.)
Row 1: ch 1 (does not count as a stitch), dc in each ch to end. Join colour B by pulling it through the final dc of the last stitch in the first group of 4. (16 sts)
From this point, carry the colour you are not using along the top of the previous row. Work the next 4 sts in B, carrying A inside the stitches.
Switch to A for the next 4 sts, carrying B. Continue to the end of the row. (16 sts)
Turn and repeat the pattern for 8 rows. The blocks align vertically to show the pattern.
Dominant colour
In tapestry crochet, the colour you pick up from below comes forward and appears slightly more prominent in the finished fabric. This is the
dominant colour
. If your pattern colour is being swallowed by the background, try reversing the pick-up order so the pattern colour is always picked from below.
Common problems

items.symptom: The carried yarn shows through between stitches
items.cause: The tension on the carried strand is too loose, allowing it to escape between stitch posts.
items.fix: Keep the carried yarn pulled gently taut as you work over it. Go down one hook size if the problem persists.

items.symptom: The fabric is pulling in at the sides
items.cause: The carried yarn is being pulled too tight, cinching the edge stitches.
items.fix: Release the tension on the carried strand before each stitch and let the working yarn fall naturally.

items.symptom: Colour pattern is visible on the wrong side
items.cause: On flat tapestry crochet worked in rows, both sides show the pattern in different forms. This is normal.
items.fix: Choose which side is the right side and stick with it. Some makers reverse the fabric deliberately to use the reverse as the public face.

content.text: What to try next

A simple tapestry pouch is a good first project: a tube worked in the round in two colours, with a geometric block motif. Working in the round keeps the right side facing at all times and produces a cleaner result than rows for beginners. Once the technique feels reliable, move to three-colour work, which requires carrying two strands at once.
